title: TP watchdog thresholds — experiments tracker (false +/-) + recommended defaults
body:
Last updated: 2025-03-06 (Sahana)

Purpose
- Track our threshold experiments for the TP-group forward-progress watchdog.
- Quantify false positives (watchdog triggers when group would have recovered) vs false negatives (hang not detected soon enough / requests time out first).
- Produce recommended defaults per deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and guidance for overrides.

Context / what we’re tuning
The watchdog implemented in runtime 1.19 (see PR-18462, PR-18473) evaluates “forward progress” for a TP group. A TP group is considered stuck when, for a window of time, it makes no measurable progress and is not simply backpressured.

We’re trying to catch:
- NCCL collectives silently stalling / async errors not surfacing quickly
- Scheduler/barrier deadlocks (esp. cancellation during streaming)
- Kernel stall cases where ranks stop advancing step counters

We must avoid triggering on:
- Legit long compute steps at long seq lengths (prefill spikes)
- Temporary comm slowdowns under overload (but still progressing)
- Multi-tenant noise in Hosted pools

Definitions
- FP (false positive): watchdog quarantines/resets TP group, but (a) progress resumes within short window without intervention OR (b) post-reset root cause indicates purely transient slowdown and the group was healthy.
- FN (false negative): user-visible timeouts/5xx from hang-like behavior occur, but watchdog did not quarantine/reset prior to SLO breach.
- “Detection lead time”: time between watchdog trigger and first customer-visible timeout avoided (positive is good).

Signal primitives (current instrumentation)
- per_rank_step_counter: monotonic counter for rank-level forward steps (approx. per microbatch / per token chunk; see PR-18462)
- collective_latency_ms histogram (allreduce/allgather/reducescatter) (PR-18455/18470)
- scheduler_queue_age_ms + runnable starvation markers (PR-18432/18470)
- watchdog_trigger_total{reason=progress_stall|collective_timeout|rank_mismatch}
- tp_group_quarantine_total and tp_group_reset_total

Knobs (names as in config draft; final names may differ)
- tp_watchdog_progress_stall_ms: if no progress observed for this long, group becomes “suspect”
- tp_watchdog_suspect_grace_ms: additional time while suspect before quarantine/reset
- tp_collective_timeout_ms: hard timeout for a single collective (if supported in path)
- tp_watchdog_min_observed_progress_delta: required delta in step counter across window
- tp_watchdog_trigger_n_consecutive_windows: number of consecutive windows before action
- tp_watchdog_action: quarantine_only | quarantine_and_teardown

Experiment methodology
Environments
- Perf-canary nightly (Hosted-like): mixed tenants, realistic traffic replay, 30–60 min runs
- Dedicated staging: single-tenant replay + stress patterns, 60 min runs
- Fault injection bench: forced rank delay, forced cancel/disconnect, induced NCCL error (where possible)

Workloads
- Mix A (typical): 70% chat streaming, 20% non-streaming, 10% embeddings; seq lengths p50=512, p95=2k
- Mix B (long-context): 40% streaming with long prompts; seq lengths p50=2k, p95=12k
- Mix C (burst): short prompts, high QPS, aggressive continuous batching

Failure injection knobs
- Delay rank k by +150ms/+300ms per step for N steps
- Random client disconnect during decode (stream cancel)
- Force collective to hang (test hook) at step boundary

Pass/fail (baseline)
- FN guard: Watchdog must trigger before 95% of request timeouts in injected hang scenarios.
- FP guard: In non-injected stress runs, watchdog triggers <= 0.02 per TP-group-hour for Hosted, <= 0.05 per TP-group-hour for Dedicated.
  - Note: FP rate limits are conservative; we’d rather miss some stalls than cause avoidable capacity churn in Hosted.

Experiment table (summary)
Columns:
- Exp ID | Date | Runtime | GPUs | Mode | Workload | Injection | progress_stall_ms | grace_ms | collective_timeout_ms | consecutive_windows | Action | Outcomes | FP rate | FN rate | Notes

EXP-01 | 2025-02-17 | 1.19.0-rc1 | H100-SXM | Hosted-like | Mix A | none | 2500 | 1500 | 2000 | 1 | quarantine+teardown | Too twitchy under bursty streams | 0.11 / group-hr | n/a | Triggered during long prefill spikes (p95>8k prompt). Not acceptable.

EXP-02 | 2025-02-18 | 1.19.0-rc1 | H100-SXM | Hosted-like | Mix A | none | 5000 | 2000 | 3000 | 1 | quarantine_only | Better, but still occasional suspect->quarantine during GC pauses on host | 0.04 / group-hr | n/a | Quarantine_only reduced disruption but still throttles capacity (group removed from scheduler).

EXP-03 | 2025-02-18 | 1.19.0-rc1 | H100-SXM | Hosted-like | Mix B | none | 6500 | 2500 | 3500 | 2 | quarantine_only | Stable for long-context | 0.015 / group-hr | n/a | No clear false triggers; higher stall threshold needed for long prefill.

EXP-04 | 2025-02-19 | 1.19.0-rc1 | H100-SXM | Hosted-like | Mix A | cancel/disconnect 2% | 6500 | 2500 | 3500 | 2 | quarantine_only | Cancellation path ok (post PR-18441 cherry-pick) | 0.018 / group-hr | 0.00 | No deadlock reproductions. Prior to PR-18441 we saw 2 hangs / 60 min.

EXP-05 | 2025-02-20 | 1.19.0-rc2 | A100-80GB | Dedicated staging | Mix A | forced rank delay +300ms | 5000 | 2000 | 2500 | 1 | quarantine+teardown | Detects injected rank lag-induced barrier stall | n/a | 0.00 | Detection lead time ~6–12s before first request timeout.

EXP-06 | 2025-02-20 | 1.19.0-rc2 | A100-80GB | Dedicated staging | Mix A | forced collective hang | 5000 | 2000 | 2500 | 1 | quarantine+teardown | Good detection but some resets during overload | 0.06 / group-hr | 0.00 | Under Mix C burst, collective latency spikes; if “no progress” coincides, we trigger.

EXP-07 | 2025-02-21 | 1.19.0-rc2 | A100-80GB | Dedicated staging | Mix C | none | 7000 | 2000 | 3000 | 2 | quarantine+teardown | Reduces overload FPs | 0.03 / group-hr | n/a | Two-window requirement helped.

EXP-08 | 2025-02-22 | 1.19.0-rc2 | L40S | Hosted-like | Mix A | none | 6500 | 2500 | 3500 | 2 | quarantine_only | Slightly higher FP vs H100 due to lower throughput variance | 0.025 / group-hr | n/a | L40S sees longer compute steps; progress counter increments less frequently.

EXP-09 | 2025-02-24 | 1.19.0-rc3 | H100-SXM | Hosted canary pool (us-east) | Mix A live | none | 6500 | 2500 | 3500 | 2 | quarantine_only | Canary looked clean; 0 customer-facing regressions | 0.009 / group-hr | n/a | Correlated: watchdog triggers coincided with host NIC error spikes (likely real stall risk).

EXP-10 | 2025-02-25 | 1.19.0-rc3 | H100-SXM | Hosted canary pool (us-east) | Mix A live | none | 8000 | 2000 | 4000 | 2 | quarantine_only | Even fewer triggers; concern about FN sensitivity | 0.004 / group-hr | TBD | Need injected hang run with these thresholds.

EXP-11 | 2025-02-26 | 1.19.0-rc3 | A100-80GB | Dedicated staging | Mix B | forced collective hang | 8000 | 2000 | 4000 | 2 | quarantine+teardown | Still catches hangs, slightly later | n/a | 0.00 | Detection lead time ~10–18s. Dedicated SLOs may tolerate.

EXP-12 | 2025-03-03 | 1.19.0 | A100-80GB | Private-like lab | Mix B | none | 8000 | 4000 | 5000 | 2 | quarantine_only | Conservative; no resets | 0.00 | n/a | Private deployments often prefer no auto-teardown; require operator visibility + runbook.

Notes on measuring FP/FN in practice
- FP classification is hard without ground truth.
  - We are treating “watchdog trigger followed by quick recovery without subsequent error signals” as likely FP.
  - If trigger coincides with elevated collective latency + rank mismatch + subsequent NCCL error, we treat as likely TP group unhealthy (true positive).
- FN measurement uses injected hangs and prod incidents with clear stall signatures (no rank progress for >60s, request timeouts rising).

Recommended defaults (proposed) — runtime 1.19+

1) Hosted (default-on; multi-tenant; prioritize minimizing FPs)
- tp_watchdog_progress_stall_ms = 6500
- tp_watchdog_suspect_grace_ms = 2500
- tp_collective_timeout_ms = 3500
- tp_watchdog_trigger_n_consecutive_windows = 2
- tp_watchdog_action = quarantine_only
Rationale:
- Achieved <= ~0.02 triggers / group-hr across H100 + L40S canaries in non-injected runs.
- Two-window requirement prevents single prefill spike from triggering.
Operational note:
- If quarantine_only repeats on same host > N times/hour, SRE may cordon host / drain pool (avoid flapping).

2) Dedicated (opt-in then default-on; single-tenant; prioritize faster recovery)
- tp_watchdog_progress_stall_ms = 7000
- tp_watchdog_suspect_grace_ms = 2000
- tp_collective_timeout_ms = 3000
- tp_watchdog_trigger_n_consecutive_windows = 2 (or 1 for customers demanding stricter recovery)
- tp_watchdog_action = quarantine_and_teardown
Rationale:
- FPs are more tolerable than sustained hung capacity (single tenant feels “everything is down”).
- Teardown helps clear “stuck but not erroring” groups.
Customer guidance:
- For long-context heavy customers (p95 prompt > 8k), start with 8000/2000/4000 and evaluate.

3) Private (default-off or quarantine_only depending on customer preference)
Option A (conservative / operator-controlled):
- watchdog enabled = true
- tp_watchdog_action = quarantine_only
- tp_watchdog_progress_stall_ms = 8000
- tp_watchdog_suspect_grace_ms = 4000
- tp_collective_timeout_ms = 5000
- tp_watchdog_trigger_n_consecutive_windows = 2
Option B (aggressive / self-healing):
- match Dedicated defaults above, but require customer sign-off + runbook readiness.
Rationale:
- Private environments vary widely; teardown may be undesirable if it impacts long-running sessions or if restart is expensive.

GPU-specific notes
- L40S: consider +1000ms to progress_stall_ms if using large continuous batches or if step counter increments less frequently.
- A100: tends to show larger variance under Mix C; keep 2 windows to reduce overload FPs.
- H100: stable; Hosted defaults above appear safe.

Open questions / TODO
- Do we need a distinct “prefill mode” threshold (larger stall window when prompt tokens in flight)? Sofia to advise based on scheduler stage signals.
- Should collective_timeout_ms scale with topology (NVLink vs PCIe)? Hiro/Grace to weigh in.
- Confirm final config naming + docs copy for release notes (Henry / Kira).

Next planned experiments
- EXP-13: Hosted thresholds from EXP-10 (8000/2000/4000, 2 windows) + injected collective hang (test hook) to assess FN risk.
- EXP-14: Dedicated, compare consecutive_windows=1 vs 2 under cancel storms (10% disconnect) to see if we regress cancellation path.
- EXP-15: Try quarantine_only + auto-drain host on repeated triggers (SRE play) vs immediate teardown.

Decision checkpoint (proposed)
- Lock Hosted defaults after EXP-13 + 1 more canary week with no SLO regression.
- Lock Dedicated defaults after EXP-14 and after validating no >1% throughput regression in perf suite (ENG-2409).

Contacts
- Runtime watchdog implementation: Samir Qureshi
- Scheduler lifecycle + quarantine semantics: Sofia Ivanova / Marcus Reed
- SRE rollout guardrails: Rafael Mendes
- Canary/CI wiring: Sahana Iyer

Changelog
- 2025-02-16: Created tracker; initial hypotheses and baseline thresholds.
- 2025-02-21: Added two-window requirement results; reduced overload FPs.
- 2025-02-26: Added Private conservative option.
- 2025-03-06: Updated recommended defaults for Hosted + Dedicated based on canary data (EXP-09..12).
